[prose] Trace plots and other diagnostics for the species richness model suggested that chains mixed well and were of sufficient length. The posterior predictive check suggested good model fit $( \chi ^ { 2 } { = } 9 3 2 . 8 7 , P { = } 0 . 4 8 )$ . Species richness increased with site surface area (Table S3, Fig. 4) but did not vary with the cover of heat islands within a 1,000 m radius around sites (Table S3). Species detection probability did not vary with sampling effort (Table S3). Detection probability followed a quadratic trend with Julian date, reaching a peak in midseason (Table S3, Fig. 5). Finally, detection probability of species with blue pan traps was lower than with yellow traps but did not differ from that of white traps (Table S3, Fig. 5).

[prose] The occupancy analysis focused on three functional groups: insectivores, terrestrial saprophagous, and aquatic saprophagous. The phytophagous functional group was excluded due to very sparse data. Trace plots and other diagnostics for the occupancy model on functional groups suggested that chains mixed well for all parameters and that chains were sufficiently long. There were no indications that the model lacked ${ \bf f } { \bf t } ,$ based on the posterior predictive check on either rows or columns $\chi^{2}{ rows } = 1096.87, P = 0.20;$ $\chi^{2}{ columns } = 7.26, P = 0.49$ . The area under the ROC curve was 0.64 (95% CRI: [0.54, 0.75]), suggesting an intermediate model performance.

[prose] Trapping occurred over 13 periods of sampling, using blue, white, and yellow coloured pan traps. Functional groups consist of insectivores (I), terrestrial saprophagous (TS), aquatic saprophagous (AS), or phytophagous (P) species
